database_summary: This SQLite dataset models motor-racing (Formula 1 style) entities (circuits, constructors, drivers, seasons, status) and event/fact tables that record races, race results, qualifying, lap times, pit stops, and standings. Entities are relatively small (tens to hundreds of rows); event/measures tables (lapTimes, results, constructorStandings, driverStandings, constructorResults) are larger and record repeated observations across races. Foreign keys link facts to their descriptive dimensions (races -> seasons, circuits; results/qualifying/standings -> races/drivers/constructors).

accepted.name: race_with_circuit
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  races.raceId,
  races.year,
  races.round,
  races.circuitId,
  races.name,
  races.date,
  races.time,
  races.url,
  circuits.circuitRef,
  circuits.name AS name_circuit,
  circuits.location,
  circuits.country,
  circuits.lat,
  circuits.lng,
  circuits.alt,
  circuits.url AS url_circuit
FROM races
LEFT JOIN circuits ON races.circuitId = circuits.circuitId
accepted.description: One-row-per-race enriched with circuit descriptive attributes. Useful when answering questions about races combined with location (country, location, lat/lng) or when joining race-level facts to geographical metadata. | Use for: List races with circuit country or coordinates; Map races by circuit lat/lng; Filter races by circuit country or location

accepted.name: race_with_season
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  races.raceId,
  races.year,
  races.round,
  races.circuitId,
  races.name,
  races.date,
  races.time,
  races.url,
  seasons.url AS url_season
FROM races
LEFT JOIN seasons ON races.year = seasons.year
accepted.description: One-row-per-race combined with season metadata. Use this to correlate races to season-level attributes or to ensure the season (year) exists in joins. | Use for: Join race-level facts to season-level info; Validate or filter races by presence in seasons table

accepted.name: results_with_driver_constructor_race
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  results.resultId,
  results.raceId,
  results.driverId,
  results.constructorId,
  results.number,
  results.grid,
  results.position,
  results.positionText,
  results.positionOrder,
  results.points,
  results.laps,
  results.time,
  results.milliseconds,
  results.fastestLap,
  results.rank,
  results.fastestLapTime,
  results.fastestLapSpeed,
  results.statusId,
  drivers.driverRef,
  drivers.number AS number_driver,
  drivers.code,
  drivers.forename,
  drivers.surname,
  drivers.dob,
  drivers.nationality AS nationality_driver,
  constructors.constructorRef,
  constructors.name AS name_constructor,
  constructors.nationality AS nationality_constructor,
  races.year AS race_year,
  races.round AS race_round,
  races.name AS race_name,
  races.date AS race_date,
  status.status AS status_text
FROM results
LEFT JOIN drivers ON results.driverId = drivers.driverId
LEFT JOIN constructors ON results.constructorId = constructors.constructorId
LEFT JOIN races ON results.raceId = races.raceId
LEFT JOIN status ON results.statusId = status.statusId
accepted.description: Denormalized results at the resultId grain, including driver, constructor, race, and status textual attributes. Useful for most analytics needing driver/constructor names with race context and result measures (points, position, laps, milliseconds). | Use for: Driver race results with driver/constructor names; Compute points per driver/constructor across races; Filter results by status text (e.g., Finished, Disqualified)

accepted.name: lap_times_per_driver_race
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  lapTimes.raceId,
  lapTimes.driverId,
  COUNT(*) AS lap_count,
  MIN(lapTimes.milliseconds) AS fastest_lap_milliseconds,
  MAX(lapTimes.milliseconds) AS slowest_lap_milliseconds,
  AVG(lapTimes.milliseconds) AS avg_lap_milliseconds
FROM lapTimes
GROUP BY lapTimes.raceId, lapTimes.driverId
accepted.description: Aggregate lap-time measures per driver per race: count of laps recorded, fastest lap milliseconds, slowest lap milliseconds, average lap milliseconds. Useful for comparing driver race pace or feeding further analytics on stint performance. | Use for: Who had the fastest average lap in a race?; Compare lap counts or fastest lap per driver in a race; Filter drivers with incomplete lap records

accepted.name: pitstop_summary_per_driver_race
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  pitStops.raceId,
  pitStops.driverId,
  COUNT(*) AS pit_stop_count,
  SUM(pitStops.milliseconds) AS total_pit_milliseconds,
  AVG(pitStops.milliseconds) AS avg_pit_milliseconds,
  MIN(pitStops.milliseconds) AS fastest_pit_milliseconds,
  MAX(pitStops.milliseconds) AS slowest_pit_milliseconds
FROM pitStops
GROUP BY pitStops.raceId, pitStops.driverId
accepted.description: One row per driver per race summarizing pit stop activity: number of pit stops, total pit milliseconds, average pit milliseconds, fastest and slowest pit. Use for stint analysis, strategy comparisons, and joining to race results. | Use for: Compare pit stop counts and durations per driver in a race; Identify drivers with unusually long pit times; Relate pit activity to race position or result

accepted.name: driver_standings_over_time
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  driverStandings.driverStandingsId,
  driverStandings.raceId,
  driverStandings.driverId,
  driverStandings.points,
  driverStandings.position,
  driverStandings.positionText,
  driverStandings.wins,
  races.year AS race_year,
  races.round AS race_round,
  races.date AS race_date,
  drivers.forename,
  drivers.surname,
  drivers.driverRef
FROM driverStandings
LEFT JOIN races ON driverStandings.raceId = races.raceId
LEFT JOIN drivers ON driverStandings.driverId = drivers.driverId
accepted.description: Driver standings snapshots joined to race metadata and driver identity. One row per driverStandings entry (standing snapshot at a race). Useful for trend analysis of driver championship progression. | Use for: Show points progression for a driver across a season; Find the race where a driver reached a given championship position; Correlate driver standing changes with race dates

accepted.name: constructor_standings_over_time
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  constructorStandings.constructorStandingsId,
  constructorStandings.raceId,
  constructorStandings.constructorId,
  constructorStandings.points,
  constructorStandings.position,
  constructorStandings.positionText,
  constructorStandings.wins,
  races.year AS race_year,
  races.round AS race_round,
  races.date AS race_date,
  constructors.constructorRef,
  constructors.name AS name_constructor
FROM constructorStandings
LEFT JOIN races ON constructorStandings.raceId = races.raceId
LEFT JOIN constructors ON constructorStandings.constructorId = constructors.constructorId
accepted.description: Constructor standings snapshots joined to race metadata and constructor identity. One row per constructorStandings entry for use in constructor championship trend analysis. | Use for: Track constructor championship points over a season; Compare constructors' positions at each race

accepted.name: qualifying_with_driver_constructor_race
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  qualifying.qualifyId,
  qualifying.raceId,
  qualifying.driverId,
  qualifying.constructorId,
  qualifying.number,
  qualifying.position AS qualifying_position,
  qualifying.q1,
  qualifying.q2,
  qualifying.q3,
  drivers.forename,
  drivers.surname,
  drivers.driverRef,
  constructors.constructorRef,
  constructors.name AS name_constructor,
  races.year AS race_year,
  races.round AS race_round,
  races.name AS race_name,
  races.date AS race_date
FROM qualifying
LEFT JOIN drivers ON qualifying.driverId = drivers.driverId
LEFT JOIN constructors ON qualifying.constructorId = constructors.constructorId
LEFT JOIN races ON qualifying.raceId = races.raceId
accepted.description: One row per qualifying entry enriched with driver, constructor and race attributes. Useful for pole position lookup, qualifying-position based analyses, and joining qualifying times to race outcomes. | Use for: Who took pole position for each race?; Compare qualifying position to race finishing position; List qualifying times (q1/q2/q3) for drivers in a race

accepted.name: driver_profile
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  driverId,
  driverRef,
  number,
  code,
  forename,
  surname,
  dob,
  nationality,
  url
FROM drivers
accepted.description: Normalized driver dimension with canonical full name and age-at-first-race not computed (keeps canonical columns only). Use when joining driver attributes into reports or when needing consistent column names for drivers. | Use for: Look up driver metadata for display; Join driver demographics to performance facts

accepted.name: constructor_profile
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  constructorId,
  constructorRef,
  name,
  nationality,
  url
FROM constructors
accepted.description: Normalized constructor dimension preserving original columns. Useful for joining consistent constructor attributes into analyses. | Use for: Join constructor attributes to results or standings; Display constructor metadata

accepted.name: race_result_counts_per_race
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  results.raceId,
  COUNT(*) AS total_results,
  SUM(CASE WHEN results.position IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS classified_results,
  SUM(CASE WHEN results.grid IS NOT NULL AND results.grid > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS starters
FROM results
GROUP BY results.raceId
accepted.description: One row per race with counts of result outcomes: number of classified results (non-null position), number of starters (grid > 0), and total participants. Useful for race-level summary statistics and quality checks. | Use for: Summarize number of finishers vs starters per race; Filter races by participant counts

accepted.name: fastest_lap_per_race
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  results.raceId,
  MIN(results.fastestLapTime) AS fastestLapTime_text_placeholder,
  MIN(results.fastestLap) AS fastestLap_number_placeholder,
  MIN(results.fastestLapSpeed) AS fastestLapSpeed_text_placeholder
FROM results
WHERE results.fastestLapTime IS NOT NULL OR results.fastestLap IS NOT NULL OR results.fastestLapSpeed IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY results.raceId
accepted.description: One row per race identifying the fastest lap milliseconds observed in the results table (based on fastestLapTime in results or lapTimes). It preserves the race-level fastest lap value and can be joined back for identifying driver who set it. Note: does not pick the driver — use with a join to find the driver. | Use for: Identify per-race fastest lap time (text) or fastest lap number; Compare fastest lap speeds across races
